children.translated_text: <s>Sarvajñasiddhi</s> (Proof of Omniscience)
Preceded by prostration at the lotus-feet of the Omniscient One (<s>Sarvajña</s>),

children.text: fehlt ein Folio; Fehler beim Fotografieren des Manuskripts.

children.translated_text: for the proof of omniscience, by us

children.text: yat pramāṇasaṃvādi niścitārthavacanaṃ tat sākṣāt parampa
children.translated_text: A statement whose determined content accords with a means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) is, either directly or through
a tradition (<s>paramparā</s>),
or
preceded by a cognition that directly perceives that [stated] object.
For example, the statement 'fire is a burner.'
And this [statement under consideration] is a statement whose content is determined by a means of valid knowledge:
'All conditioned things (<s>saṃskāra</s>) are momentary' — this, in substance, is a [valid] reason based on effect (<s>kāryahetu</s>).
There is no unestablishedness (<s>asiddhi</s>) of this [reason], since all entities are proven to be momentary (<s>kṣaṇabhaṅga</s>) — because this statement
has a true content.
Nor is there contradiction (<s>virodha</s>), since [the reason] is present in the positive instance (<s>sapakṣa</s>).
Nor is it inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>): although a mere statement can be preceded by doubt or error,
a statement whose content is determined by a means of valid knowledge is, either directly or through a tradition,
or
that object —
preceded by a cognition that directly perceives [it]; otherwise there would be no invariable
accordance
with a valid means of knowledge

children.text: was auch das letzte von Ratnakīrti zitierte Wort ist. Da der
-Text inhaltlich diesen Beweis voraussetzt und logisch fortfährt, liegt die Annahme nahe, daß das fehlende Folio den obigen bei Ratnakīrti zitierten Beweis enthalten hat.
na tv asmadādīnāṃ kṣaṇabhaṅgasādhanam anumānam utpadyate | na
children.translated_text: However, the inference (<s>anumāna</s>) proving momentariness does not arise for people like us; nor

children.text: ca tadviṣayam adhyakṣaṃ vidyate | tad api pratyakṣadarśipu
children.translated_text: is there direct perception (<s>adhyakṣa</s>) having that [momentariness] as its object. Yet even that [inference] arises through the instruction of a person who sees directly (<s>pratyakṣadarśin</s>)
so through tradition, it is preceded by direct perception
alone.
of this [inference], whose origination depends on the proof,
how can it be preceded by another's instruction? — if [objected] thus:
[The reason] whose birth depends on the proof, [which has] a pervasion established by a sublating valid cognition (<s>bādhaka-pramāṇa</s>) —

children.text: yadi paropadeśo na syād kiṃ siddhaṃ kṣaṇabhaṅgi āhosvid
akṣaṇikam iti saṃśaya eva na syāt | asati cāsmin na sādhanaṃ
children.translated_text: non-momentary?' would simply not arise. And in the absence of that [doubt], the proof
would not proceed.
If another's instruction did not exist, the doubt 'Is what is established momentary or

children.text: nanu paropadeśam antareṇāpi saṃśayo bhavan kena vāryeta

children.translated_text: [It would be prevented] by a cause of error.
[Objection:] Surely, even without another's instruction, doubt that arises — by what could it be prevented?
even when the occasion [for inference] is present, for a dull-witted person who has been deceived by a non-direct perception that resembles [direct perception],
the mistaken

children.text: labdhasya mandabuddheḥ sa evāyam iti pūrvāparikatvādhyavasāyo
children.translated_text: determination 'this is the very same [thing]' — the conviction that [things have] identity between earlier and later —
never
changes. How could the doubt about whether that [thing] is [momentary] or not arise without another's instruction,
come
into being?
[Regarding] inference
But that it must be from one who sees directly (<s>pratyakṣadarśin</s>) alone —

children.text: tu kutaḥ | anumātur apy upadeśād asau bhavann upapanna eva |
children.translated_text: whence [is that claimed]? Even from the instruction of one who infers (<s>anumātṛ</s>), that [doubt] arising is indeed reasonable.
Granted, doubt arises from another's instruction.

children.text: nanu tasyāpy anumātur anumānodayahetuḥ saṃśayaḥ kuta iti

children.translated_text: [from where does it come?]
[Reply:] Surely, for that inferrer too, the source of the doubt that causes the arising of inference must be stated —
If [you say] from the instruction of another inferrer —
because the same objection applies there as well.
no,
If [you say] there is no fault since the doubt of each successive inferrer is preceded by the instruction of a beginningless [series of] prior inferrers —
because for all [persons], the connection with ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) is the same, and this non-direct perception resembling [direct perception]
is the cause of the erroneous [conviction] under dispute,
[and since this cause] is common [to all], the cause of the doubt that is the reason for inference
[namely, doubt]
has no scope in a mind that is not free from the contrary error — therefore inferrer-hood would be impossible. For if there were some instructor who had seen directly,

children.text: tvāyogāt | yadi hi sākṣāddraṣṭā kaścid upadeṣṭā bhavet

children.translated_text: then there would be
doubt arising from his instruction, [and] some [person would become] an inferrer;
from [that inferrer's] instruction
[there would arise] doubt;
other persons too would
become
inferrers. But in the absence of a person who has seen directly,
since there is no arising of non-erroneous tendencies (<s>vāsanā</s>) in the knower — and hence no convention (<s>samaya</s>) — and hence no arising
of inference [at all],

children.text: katham anumātṛtvaṃ nama | tasmāt sākṣāddraṣṭopadeṣṭā kaścid
children.translated_text: how could there be inferrer-hood? Therefore, some instructor who has seen directly must be accepted. And whoever is an instructor who directly perceives the momentariness of all <s>dharmas</s> and the like —
that is the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One),
the crest-jewel of gods and <s>asuras</s>, the Omniscient One (<s>Sarvajña</s>).
no,

children.text: kṛtvā sarvavidaḥ siddhiṃ puṇyam āsāditaṃ mayā |
children.translated_text: Having accomplished the proof of the All-Knowing One, the merit attained by me —

children.text: etena sakalo lokaḥ sārvajñaṃ padam āpnuyāt ||
children.translated_text: by this, may the entire world attain the state of omniscience (<s>sārvajña</s>)!
|| The <s>Sarvajñasiddhi</s> (Proof of Omniscience) of the learned <s>Jitāri</s> [is complete]. ||
